holding_summary: A zoning ordinance barring most business on a residential street, but expressly exempting drug stores, boarding houses, apartment houses, hotels, and banks, was upheld against a claim of arbitrary discrimination. The court reasoned the exempted uses were less objectionable than ordinary commerce, or were necessary conveniences for the neighborhood.

quotes.text: The exceptions may very well rest upon the favored establishments being not so objectionable as other business establishments, or may rest upon the necessity of having a drug store, boarding house, apartment house, hotel, and a branch bank in the neighborhood.

No payment or lodging/boarding characterization is at issue -- this is a mistaken-boundary trespass case, not compensated occupancy.
Personal-injury trespasser/licensee case involving boys sleeping on a saw-mill boiler; no dwelling-letting issue.

holding_summary: A mother who furnished board and lodging in her own home to her adult, abandoned daughter could recover the value of that lodging and board from the absent husband under an implied quasi-contract for necessaries. The court treated a one-year prescription for actions by 'innkeepers and such others on account of lodging and board' as applicable in principle but found the suit timely regardless.

quotes.text: Obviously, lodging and board were indispensable necessaries to Mrs. Barr which were legally furnished by her mother and for which defendant is bound by an implied or quasi-contract.

notes: Actual occupancy ran from May 1918 to July 1925 (roughly seven years), which exceeds the nights/weeks/months categories provided; marked duration_of_occupancy unclear rather than force it into 'months.' Arrangement is family (mother-daughter) lodging/board rather than a stranger-lodger, but the court expressly analogizes the claim to statutory 'lodging and board' actions against innkeepers, so it bears on the legal character of compensated lodging arrangements.
